subject: Re: FulcrumAI: sudden p99 TTFT regressions — possible upstream handshake timeouts
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@fulcrumai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: TTFT regressions - p95/p99 spikes since 02/18 06:40 UTC

Kimberly,

We're seeing a sudden regression in first-token latency for our production calls through the Redwood hosted API starting ~06:40 UTC this morning. p95 moved from ~180ms to ~650ms and p99 is spiking to ~1.2s. Error rate hasn't increased much yet but saw a small bump in 5xxs (~0.6%).

Attached is a Puppeteer capture and a small set of traces where the client shows long TLS handshake times (~600-800ms) before any bytes are returned. The traces point to a handful of edge POPs in us-west and us-central.

We need to understand whether this is an issue on your side (CDN/handshake) or something upstream. Can we get an immediate point of contact to triage? We're trying to avoid user-visible timeouts — several sessions saw timeouts at 2s.

Attachments: fulcrum-pptr-trace-20270218.json

Thanks,
Alex Nguyen
Senior SRE, FulcrumAI
alex.nguyen@fulcrumai.com

Subject: Re: TTFT regressions - p95/p99 spikes since 02/18 06:40 UTC

Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the trace. I'm escalating immediately to eng and ops. Proposed next steps: 

- 9:35 AM PT quick sync (30 min) to triage live traces and agree mitigation. Calendar invite: https://cal.redwood.com/meet/kimberly/fulcrum-triage
- Engineering to run targeted packet captures and look at TLS handshake latency distribution across POPs
- If it's an upstream CDN edge issue, we can failover routing for Fulcrum to alternate POPs until fixed

I've looped in Marcus, Karthik and Marissa. Marcus — can you lead triage and suggest an immediate mitigation we can apply (routing, short TTL changes, or temporary origin pinning)?

Kimberly Park
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@fulcrumai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:46:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: TTFT regressions - p95/p99 spikes since 02/18 06:40 UTC

Quick status from infra: we've reproduced the p99 TTFT increases in our telemetry. Early signal shows an elevated TLS handshake duration from a subset of CDN edge POPs (predominantly us-west-2 and us-central-1). Observations: 

- SYN/ACK completes quickly but TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello time is elevated (300-900ms) in ~4% of connections for Fulcrum traces.
- Packet captures show retransmits and a burst of handshake retries to specific edge IPs — suggests an overloaded or degraded upstream edge node performing TLS ops slowly.
- No obvious cert expiration event on our side. Kernel and crypto stacks look healthy.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (pick one or combine):
1) Traffic steering: route Fulcrum traffic away from impacted POPs to alternate edges (us-east-1 / us-east-2). This is low risk and reversible.
2) Short TTL for edge DNS for their zone to accelerate re-resolution.
3) If needed, pin Fulcrum to direct origin for a limited window to bypass CDN edge handshake (higher egress cost, minimal change window).

I'll attach a short sample of the handshake timing for the affected IPs (handshake-samples.txt) and open RED-8132 to track. Marcus.

Attachments: handshake-samples.txt
Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-8132
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@fulcrumai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: TTFT regressions - p95/p99 spikes since 02/18 06:40 UTC

Alex — thanks Marcus. We can push traffic steering immediately. Proposed mitigation window: route Fulcrum traffic to us-east POPs starting 10:15 AM PT for an initial 12 hour window while infra completes deeper root-cause analysis. Expected impact: p99 should return close to baseline for most requests; if you see lingering outliers we can escalate to origin pinning.

Please confirm you are OK with the temporary routing. We will monitor 1-min metrics and revert as soon as we see stability. I'll also prepare an incident brief and follow up on potential SLA credit conversations if impact persists.

Kimberly

Subject: FYI: FulcrumAI TTFT spike and mitigation (routing applied) — exec summary

Team — quick exec summary for visibility: 

- Incident: Starting 2027-02-18 06:40 UTC, FulcrumAI experienced p95/p99 first-token latency regressions tied to elevated TLS handshake durations at a subset of CDN edges (us-west-2/us-central).
- Action taken: On 2027-02-18 10:15 PT we steered Fulcrum traffic to alternate us-east POPs; immediate improvement in p99 observed (~from 1.2s to ~240ms).
- Customer impact: transient user-visible delays for select sessions; Fulcrum notified and has approved the routing mitigation. Procurement may open a credit request; tracking under DL-2026-7789.
- Next steps: deep post-mortem with infra (RED-8132), remediation to remove root cause on affected edge hosts, and a customer-facing timeline for fixes and any credits.

Link to incident brief: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/ops/fulcrum/handshake-analysis-20270218.pdf

I'll schedule the PM/infra post-mortem for early next week.

Kimberly Park
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
